title: Vidyorja Scholars' Institute multi-branch roadside banner run: neutralize eight differently-lit branch student photos to one house white point against an in-frame grey card, prep-and-vectorize the flat subject-icon art, cut out and deepen the painted crest, author a brand duotone geometric texture, and data-merge one press-ready CMYK banner per branch
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com roadside coaching-institute banner brief (a local tutoring institute wanting a 'clean, premium, professional' large-format flex banner that stays readable from the road, with subject-hinting icons, a confident-but-minimal photo of students, understated geometric elements, and a print-ready CMYK PDF) and laundered to a fictional brand, 'Vidyorja Scholars' Institute' — a coined name, not a real company, school, product, person, or trademark; all branch localities are generic address strings, not real institutions. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: layout COMPOSITION from scratch is not connector-doable (the connector cannot typeset a banner, place images at coordinates, or draw shapes), so the layered banner is modeled as a genuinely hand-authored InDesign SINGLE-RECORD banner template (.indd, explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output) carrying live <<fields>> and FOUR @-prefixed image-path columns; the institute is running a synchronized eight-branch 'ADMISSIONS OPEN' campaign, so the connector-doable deliverable is exactly what document_merge_data_layout genuinely produces — ONE banner per branch (one record per page). The real paid work the Adobe chain rewards: bring eight branch-supplied student photos, each shot locally under different light with an 18% grey card in frame, to ONE consistent institute-house white point (so the campaign reads as one set) by reasoning a separate correction for each frame; prep-and-vectorize the flat subject-icon art to crisp print SVG; recognize that a second supplied 'mark' is a PHOTOGRAPH of the painted crest (not flat art) and cut it out, then deepen its faded paint to the brand deep-blue by an in-family masked recolor; author an understated brand duotone geometric texture from a supplied architectural surface; and merge the authored template against the branch roster into a press-ready CMYK banner run. The brand blues are applied ONLY where a connector can honestly apply them (a whole-image tint of a texture field, an in-family deepen of an already-blue crest, and the template's own flat brand field) — the student photos are never swung to a specific brand hex, which no connector can do on varied pixels.
one_line_ask: Bring eight branch student photos shot under different light to one consistent institute-house look by neutralizing each to the 18% grey card it carries and deciding the correction per frame, prep and vectorize the flat subject-icon art, cut out the photographed painted crest and deepen it to the brand deep-blue in its own color family, author an understated brand duotone geometric texture, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign banner template against the eight-branch roster into one press-ready CMYK banner per branch.
full_brief:
Vidyorja Scholars' Institute is opening admissions across eight branches at once and needs a synchronized roadside flex-banner campaign — one 10 ft x 5 ft (2:1) banner per branch, each carrying that branch's own students but every banner unmistakably part of ONE campaign. We have hand-built the InDesign banner template with all the fixed copy laid out (institute name, tagline 'Where Effort Meets Merit', the course list, ADMISSIONS OPEN, the feature bullets) and left live placeholder fields for the per-branch lines (branch name, area/landmark address, and the branch phone numbers) plus reserved picture frames for the branch hero photo, the subject icons, the institute crest, and a background texture. We are NOT reshooting anything. Here is the real problem and the reason this is not a five-minute job:

1) The eight branch photos are a mismatched jumble. Each branch shot its own group of students on whatever it had — some rooms are lit by cool white tube-lights, some by warm afternoon window light, a couple came in underexposed, one is blown out and warm, and several frames are slightly crooked. Straight out of the folder they look like eight different campaigns. To make 'matched' checkable we had every branch lay a photographic 18% grey card into a corner of the frame. Your job: bring every photo to ONE consistent institute-house look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — in your finished frame that card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) — and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point. Hold a subtle, warm, welcoming institute feel in the final look, but do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each photo was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure, and tone decision to land on the shared target. Be careful — at least one branch room is genuinely warm (wood-panelled, warm afternoon light is the real character of the space) and was shot under neutral light, so its grey card already reads neutral; if you 'cool' it chasing an imagined cast you will strip the real warmth the space actually has. Two of the branches shot what looks like the same style of classroom, but one is under cool tubes and the other under warm window light — they need OPPOSITE corrections even though they look alike. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm the set is matched, not eyeballed.

2) We are handing you two brand 'marks' to prepare, and they are not the same kind of file even though we named them the same way — open both and decide what each one actually is before you touch it, because the right treatment for one is the wrong treatment for the other and getting it backwards produces garbage that only shows up at full print size. One is the clean subject-icon art (the little beaker/sigma/globe/book symbols that hint at the subjects) and it must end up as crisp, infinitely-scalable print vector so it stays sharp on a ten-foot banner. The other is our institute crest, and its paint has faded; we want it deepened to our brand deep-blue — but it must stay the crest, with its real surface and edges intact, not turned into a flat blob or a rectangle.

3) Build the understated geometric element. We want a quiet two-tone brand-blue background texture — not a loud pattern — derived from the architectural surface photo we included; make it read as a designed brand accent in our blues, subtle enough to sit behind type.

4) Finally, produce the banners. Merge our authored template against the branch roster so every branch gets its own single banner: its branch name, area line and phone numbers bound from the roster, its matching house-graded hero photo dropped into the hero frame, and the shared prepared crest, subject icons and brand texture dropped into their frames — then hand back one press-ready CMYK PDF for large-format flex printing covering all eight branches, one banner per page. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our lines or invent phone numbers.

Our brand deep-blue is a deep signal-blue (target ~#0B4F8A) with a bright sky-blue support (~#2AA8E0); apply those blues only where they honestly belong — the texture, the crest, and the template's own brand field. Do NOT try to paint the student photos into the brand blue; we want the students true-to-life and simply matched to one clean, subtly-warm house look. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point with the warm-room branch not stripped; the subject icons a clean skew-free vector; the crest a clean cutout deepened within its own blue family with its surface intact; the texture a quiet two-tone brand accent; and exactly one press-ready CMYK banner per branch, page-count equal to branch-count.

inputs.name: branch_banner_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 10 ft x 5 ft (2:1) large-format roadside banner — ONE branch per page. It carries the fixed campaign copy already typeset in a bold sans headline family (institute name 'Vidyorja Scholars' Institute', tagline 'Where Effort Meets Merit', the course list Pre-Foundation / Class 9-10 / Class 11-12, 'ADMISSIONS OPEN', and the four feature bullets Small Batch Size / Personal Attention / Regular Tests / Doubt Sessions), plus LIVE InDesign data-merge placeholder fields for the per-branch lines: <<branch_name>>, <<area_line>>, <<phone_primary>>, <<phone_secondary>>, and FOUR @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to four separate picture frames: a hero frame bound to @hero (that branch's house-graded student photo), an icons frame on a LIGHT panel bound to @icons (the shared vectorized subject-icon SVG), a crest frame on a LIGHT panel bound to @crest (the shared prepared crest cutout), and a full-bleed background frame bound to @texture (the shared brand duotone texture). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, every prepared asset reaches the banner ONLY as a merge bind through one of these four image frames. Built by hand in InDesign so all fields and all four image frames actually bind; CMYK document intent for flex print. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one branch's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record banner is the correct, connector-doable shape and 'one banner per branch' equals page-count = row-count. Supplied as an input, never a chain output; a convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced. FOUR image columns mean the merge resolves four prepped assets per row — the row's house-graded hero via @hero and the three shared assets (icons SVG, crest cutout, duotone texture) identical in every row — so the chain-produced vectors/cutout/texture reach every banner as a merge bind, never as banned free-form placement. The icons and crest frames sit on a LIGHT panel by design so any enclosed counters left filled by remove_background read as white (no dark-ground knockout is required or claimed).

inputs.name: branch_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns branch_name,area_line,phone_primary,phone_secondary,@hero,@icons,@crest,@texture holding 8 branch rows: Nandanvan, Sabari Nagar, Deepganga, Hariyali Chowk, Sundar Colony, Meghdoot Nagar, Kirti Marg, Suryodaya Block. Each row carries a plausible fictional area/landmark line (e.g. 'Opp. Water Tank, Station Road, Nandanvan') and two obviously-fictional +91 phone numbers (e.g. +91 90000 01001 / +91 90000 01002 — all clearly placeholder). The @hero column names the branch's prepared hero file in row order (@hero_01.jpg for Nandanvan, @hero_02.jpg for Sabari Nagar, ... @hero_08.jpg for Suryodaya Block) so the [T] merge drops each house-graded photo into that branch's hero frame. The @icons column holds the SAME vectorized icon file (@subject_icons.svg) in EVERY row, @crest holds the SAME crest cutout (@crest_cutout_brandblue.png) in every row, and @texture holds the SAME duotone texture (@brand_duotone_texture.png) in every row, so the three shared assets drop onto every branch's banner as merge binds. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<branch_name>>,<<area_line>>,<<phone_primary>>,<<phone_secondary>> and the four @image-path columns @hero,@icons,@crest,@texture.
inputs.realism_notes: Honors the brief's per-branch personalization; headers match the authored .indd fields and all four @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy plus the four assets per branch. The roster carries NO treatment hint — it does not say which capture is tilted, warm, the trap, or which mark is flat art vs a photo; the @hero values map to agent-produced outputs in plain row order only. @icons/@crest/@texture carry identical shared paths in all eight rows (mirrors AO-74's shared-@Wordmark pattern). Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished banners.

inputs.name: branch_captures_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera), each showing a small group of coaching-institute students (mixed ages 12-17, mixed genders, holding notebooks) in a classroom, with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, clearly visible and uncropped in each. Named neutrally capture_01.jpg ... capture_08.jpg with NO descriptive suffixes. Shot at eight branches under mismatched light: (01) cool white tube-light room, frame tilted ~+3.5 deg; (02) warm afternoon window light, level; (03) a genuinely WARM wood-panelled room whose warmth is the real character of the space, but shot under near-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the room, not a white-balance error), level; (04) flat and underexposed room, level; (05) cool tube-light classroom, tilted ~-4 deg; (06) a classroom that looks like the SAME style room as 05 but lit by warm window light, level; (07) overexposed and warm room, level; (08) near-neutral light, slightly tilted ~+2 deg. Every frame has real skin texture, stray hairs, correct hands, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each hero crop can fill the banner's hero frame by DOWNSCALE ONLY at large-format effective resolution — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure, and tilt all vary) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision toward the one shared white point. The in-frame 18% grey card is the free, checkable neutral target. THE TRAP is capture_03: its warmth is the real room, its card is already neutral, so cooling it strips real color — the correct move holds white balance. capture_05 and capture_06 are the decoy pair — they look like the same room but are lit oppositely (cool vs warm) and need OPPOSITE corrections. Filenames carry NO hint of any of this; the agent must open each frame and reason. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.

inputs.name: mark_01.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop SCAN of a subject-icon sheet inked on off-white textured paper: six minimal single-weight brand-blue line icons hinting at school subjects arranged in a 3x2 grid — a beaker (Science), a sigma symbol (Maths), a globe (Social Science), an open book (English), a DNA helix (Biology), a balance scale (Commerce). Uniform stroke weight, generous padding, no text labels. Rendered as a real scan: the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole sheet sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around the grid, and edges are a touch soft. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it vectorizes cleanly. ~2400 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: This is FLAT LINE ART on paper — the correct treatment is prep-before-trace then image_vectorize into a clean SVG. Deliberately shares the neutral 'mark_0N.png' naming and file kind with mark_02 so the agent cannot tell from the filename which mark is flat art and which is a photograph — it must open both and decide. Off-white ground + slight skew + margin force genuine prep (straighten, crisp, crop-to-bounds, knock-to-transparency) before tracing, or the trace bakes in the paper and the skew. On the banner the icons sit on a LIGHT panel, so any enclosed counters left filled read as white.

inputs.name: mark_02.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A real close-up PHOTOGRAPH of the institute's painted crest emblem mounted on a signboard: a hand-painted circular crest (a lamp-and-open-book device with a ribbon), the PAINT VISIBLY FADED to a dull teal-blue, with genuine surface texture — brush strokes, slight sheen, a faint cast shadow, minor weathering — photographed slightly off-square against a plain wall under even daylight, ~3000 px on the long edge. This is a photo of a physical painted object, NOT flat vector-style art.
inputs.realism_notes: This is a PHOTOGRAPH of a physical painted crest — the correct treatment is a CUTOUT (isolate the emblem as the subject to transparency via image_remove_background), NOT a trace: feeding a photograph to image_vectorize returns a black silhouette / garbage paths, which is the exact triage trap. Shares the neutral 'mark_0N.png' kind/name with mark_01 so the distinction is only discoverable by opening it. Its faded teal-blue paint must be deepened toward the brand deep-blue by an IN-FAMILY masked recolor (image_adjust_hsl: teal ~180 deg -> deep signal-blue ~215 deg is a small in-band shift well under 90 deg, plus a luminance/saturation settle) riding the paint's own luminosity so brush texture, sheen and shadow survive — NOT image_apply_color_overlay (whole-image, would tint the transparency/edges) and NOT image_fill_area (flat dead-fill, kills the surface). On the banner the crest sits on a LIGHT panel.

inputs.name: surface_ref.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A real photograph of a repeating architectural surface suitable as a quiet background texture: an even grid of building window louvres / a concrete brise-soleil facade shot straight-on in soft daylight, regular geometric rhythm, neutral grey concrete tones, ~3500 px on the long edge, no people, no signage, no logos.
inputs.realism_notes: The raw material for the agent-AUTHORED brand duotone geometric texture. The agent reasons the two-tone separation from primitives (image_apply_adjustments to crush the mid-tones toward a near-two-value tonal base, then image_apply_monochromatic_tint toward the brand deep-blue, then a touch of image_add_grain for print tooth) — a designed accent the agent owns, not a preset or a canned filter default. Geometric/architectural (not a student photo) so the 'understated geometric element' is honest.

outputs.name: Vidyorja_BranchBanners_x8_PRINT.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready CMYK large-format banner pages — ONE single-record 10 ft x 5 ft (2:1) banner per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each banner binds its branch_name/area_line/phone_primary/phone_secondary verbatim from the roster with its matching house-graded hero photo in the hero frame (via @hero) and the three shared assets — the vectorized subject icons (via @icons), the deepened crest cutout (via @crest) and the brand duotone texture (via @texture) — all by merge bind, never free-form placement. Large-format flex effective resolution (design-scale, downscale-only from camera-scale sources; effective PPI at each hero frame at or above the flex-print floor, no upscaling). PRIMARY DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: branch_hero_photos_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened branch student photos, delivered as the hero-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge via @hero_01.jpg..@hero_08.jpg, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while holding a subtle warm institute tone, and true-to-life (the genuinely-warm branch not stripped); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered hero crop (grey card fully cropped OUT, no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the hero crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each of the eight frames.

outputs.name: subject_icons.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the six subject icons, traced only AFTER the scanned sheet is straightened, crisped, cropped to the icon bounds, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at ten-foot banner scale with no captured paper ground or skew. Sits on the template's light icons panel.

outputs.name: crest_cutout_brandblue.png
outputs.spec: Transparent-PNG cutout of the photographed institute crest emblem (isolated via image_remove_background, NOT traced), its faded teal-blue paint deepened to the brand deep-blue (~#0B4F8A) by an IN-FAMILY masked image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small in-band teal->deep-blue hue settle plus a saturation/luminance move, no near-complementary rotation) riding the paint's own luminosity so the brush texture, sheen and cast shadow stay intact — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill. Sits on the template's light crest panel.

outputs.name: brand_duotone_texture.png
outputs.spec: An agent-authored quiet two-tone brand-blue geometric background texture built from the architectural surface photo via reasoned primitives (a tonal crush to a near-two-value base, a monochromatic deep-blue tint, a touch of print grain) — an understated designed accent in the institute blues, subtle enough to sit full-bleed behind the banner type.

connector_workflow.note: Triage step: capture_01 is tilted ~+3.5 deg, so level it first (only the tilted frames 01/05/08 get straightened; deciding which are tilted is part of the job — image_auto_straighten is the ONLY rectify tool).

Cool tube-light cast: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and hold a subtle warm institute tone. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do not reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitives call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast).

Crop the neutralized frame to the banner hero frame aspect, framing on the students with the grey card cropped OUT — this hero crop (card removed) binds into Nandanvan's banner via @hero_01.jpg. The pre-crop cap01_neutralized (card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion is the separate check here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.

Level frame, warm window light: COOL it (negative temperature) to neutralize its grey card and match the shared white point established on frame 01. Distinct numbers from frame 01 because the light differed — opposite direction. Report the move.
Crop to the banner hero frame (grey card cropped OUT) for Sabari Nagar's @hero_02.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. The room is genuinely warm (wood-panelled) and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction from frames 01/05, or that 'cools an imagined warm cast', will neutralize the card off-neutral and strip the real warmth of the space. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop to the banner hero frame (grey card cropped OUT) for Deepganga's @hero_03.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Flat and underexposed, level: the dominant move here is TONAL — lift exposure and add contrast/clarity — then a small WB nudge to land its grey card on the shared white point. Different problem from the cool/warm frames. Report the move.
Crop to the banner hero frame (grey card cropped OUT) for Hariyali Chowk's @hero_04.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~-4 deg under cool tube light — level it. (Decoy pair with frame 06: looks like the same room but is lit oppositely.)

Cool cast: WARM it to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Even though this room looks like frame 06's room, it is lit COOL and must move the OPPOSITE direction from 06 — proof the batch needs per-frame reasoning, not a blanket pass. Report the move.
Crop to the banner hero frame (grey card cropped OUT) for Sundar Colony's @hero_05.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

The decoy twin of frame 05: same-looking room but WARM window light, level. COOL it to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point — opposite direction from frame 05 despite the visual similarity. An agent that copies frame 05's warm-up here leaves this frame blue. Report the move.
Crop to the banner hero frame (grey card cropped OUT) for Meghdoot Nagar's @hero_06.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Overexposed and warm, level: PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown room first, then COOL to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Opposite tonal AND WB direction from the underexposed frame 04. Report the move.
Crop to the banner hero frame (grey card cropped OUT) for Kirti Marg's @hero_07.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Slightly tilted ~+2 deg — level it.

Near-neutral light: its grey card is close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge is needed to land on the shared white point — over-correcting would push it off the matched set. Set exposure to match the set brightness, hold the warm institute tone. Report the (small) move. Frames 01-08 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Crop to the banner hero frame (grey card cropped OUT) for Suryodaya Block's @hero_08.jpg. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

TRIAGE: on opening, mark_01 is FLAT LINE ART scanned on paper — the correct path is prep-before-trace -> vectorize (NOT a cutout). Prep step 1: the sheet sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the brand-blue strokes separate hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the icon grid so vectorize traces only the icons, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the icon strokes only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). Enclosed counters left filled will read as white on the banner's light icons panel.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the banner icons frame. Tracing the raw scan — or worse, tracing the photographed crest mark_02 — would produce skewed, paper-bounded or black-silhouette garbage; this prep chain plus the mark_01-vs-mark_02 triage is the discipline being tested.

TRIAGE: on opening, mark_02 is a PHOTOGRAPH of the painted crest emblem — the correct path is a CUTOUT, NOT a trace. Isolate the crest as the subject to transparency via remove_background. Feeding this photo to image_vectorize would return a black silhouette — the trap the mark_01/mark_02 triage guards against. remove_background isolates the outer surround only; the light crest panel on the banner means no enclosed-counter knockout is needed.

Semantically select the painted emblem artwork ('the painted crest emblem') on the cutout to scope the recolor to the emblem's paint. A named object, not a hue or a coordinate region. Returns a maskURI for the in-family deepen.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes cutout + mask): settle the faded teal (~180 deg) a short way into the brand deep-blue family (~215 deg) — a small IN-BAND hue move well under 90 deg (NOT a near-complementary rotation) — while letting the paint's existing luminosity carry the brush texture, sheen and cast shadow. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the transparency and edges) and image_fill_area is flat dead-fill (kills the painted surface) — both wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): drop the blue-band luminance and settle saturation so the emblem lands on the rich brand deep-blue (~#0B4F8A) instead of a pale washed teal, still riding the original luminosity so surface, sheen and shadow stay natural. A deepen-and-settle in the same blue family, not a swing to a new hue. DELIVERABLE crest cutout, transparent ground.

Agent-authored look step 1: reason a near-two-value tonal base from the architectural surface — push contrast hard, crush the blacks and lift the whites so the geometric rhythm reads as two masses, then set exposure so the texture is quiet enough to sit behind type. This tonal separation is the agent's design decision, not a preset.

Agent-authored look step 2: tint the two-tone base toward the brand deep-blue (~#0B4F8A) so the geometry reads in the institute blues — a duotone accent. Whole-image tint is correct here because the whole texture field should carry the brand blue (this is a texture, not a masked recolor).

Agent-authored look step 3: add a touch of print grain so the flat duotone has tooth and does not band on large-format flex. DELIVERABLE brand duotone geometric texture, ready for the banner's full-bleed @texture frame.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: hero_01, hero_02, hero_03, hero_04, hero_05, hero_06, hero_07, hero_08, subject_icons.svg, crest_cutout_brandblue.png, brand_duotone_texture.png
connector_workflow.note: Initialize one upload session for the eight house-graded hero crops plus the three shared assets (icons SVG, crest cutout, duotone texture) so the merge can resolve them by the four @-image columns. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references (@hero_01.jpg..@hero_08.jpg, @subject_icons.svg, @crest_cutout_brandblue.png, @brand_duotone_texture.png).
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's four @-image columns resolve to — the per-branch hero and the three shared assets — for each single-record banner's four picture frames.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (branch_name/area_line/phone_primary/phone_secondary) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve all FOUR image columns per row — that branch's house-graded hero into @hero, plus the shared vectorized icons (@icons), deepened crest cutout (@crest) and brand duotone texture (@texture, identical in every row) into their frames — producing EXACTLY ONE merged banner per row (eight banners). Binding the prepared assets through the image columns is the ONLY connector-doable path onto the banner: free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its four merge-wired image frames; a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind, and a multi-record grid is impossible.

Export the merged single-record banners to a press-ready CMYK large-format PDF, one banner per branch. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight banners, one page per branch) in a single call — it cannot export one named branch on its own, so any 'hero branch' is simply one page of this set. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. PRIMARY DELIVERABLE.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout.
